# RegionEditCommand&lt;TPixel&gt;

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Editing` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public abstract class RegionEditCommand<TPixel> : IEditCommand<TPixel>
```

Base for edits expressed as "these pixels get these new values". The new pixels are computed once, before any mutation, and the prior pixels are snapshotted for undo — so redo is just Apply again. Region-scoped, so history stays memory-light even on a large canvas.

**Type parameters**

- `TPixel` - The pixel the target surface stores.

## Remarks

Generic over the pixel rather than duplicated per surface specifically because of the undo snapshot: two copies of that could diverge silently and corrupt history rather than failing to compile. It is also where the [`OpacityLock`](Nfty.Core.Editing.OpacityLock.md) is enforced — on the way into `_after`, so *every* command obeys, including ones that take their alpha from the surface (flood fill's seed match, move's copied pixels) rather than from a brush, and including any command written later that never thinks about opacity at all.

## Methods

### Admit(IEditSurface&lt;TPixel&gt;, TPixel) { #m-admit-nfty-core-editing-ieditsurface-0-0 }

```csharp
protected TPixel Admit(IEditSurface<TPixel> surface, TPixel pixel);
```

The pixel as this edit is actually allowed to write it: unchanged when unlocked, alpha snapped to 255 or 0 when locked. [`RegionEditCommand<TPixel>.Apply()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.RegionEditCommand-1.md#m-apply-nfty-core-editing-ieditsurface-0) puts every computed pixel through this, so a subclass never has to; it is exposed only so a command can ask "would this write change anything?" before doing expensive work, and it is idempotent, so asking twice is harmless.

**Parameters**

- `surface` (`IEditSurface<TPixel>`) - The surface being edited; knows where its pixel keeps its alpha.
- `pixel` (`TPixel`) - The pixel the edit computed.

**Returns.** The pixel the opacity mode admits.

### Apply(IEditSurface&lt;TPixel&gt;) { #m-apply-nfty-core-editing-ieditsurface-0 }

```csharp
public bool Apply(IEditSurface<TPixel> surface);
```

Applies the edit, snapshotting the pixels it is about to overwrite so [`RegionEditCommand<TPixel>.Undo()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.RegionEditCommand-1.md#m-undo-nfty-core-editing-ieditsurface-0) can put them back.

**Parameters**

- `surface` (`IEditSurface<TPixel>`) - The surface to edit.

**Returns.** True when the edit changed anything.

### StampDiscs(IEditSurface&lt;TPixel&gt;, IReadOnlyList&lt;(int, int)&gt;, int, Func&lt;int, int, TPixel&gt;) { #m-stampdiscs-nfty-core-editing-ieditsurface-0-system-col-ed26e7 }

```csharp
protected static List<(int, int, TPixel)> StampDiscs(IEditSurface<TPixel> surface, IReadOnlyList<(int, int)> path, int size, Func<int, int, TPixel> paint);
```

Stamps a filled round disc of diameter `size` along `path`, visiting each in-bounds pixel at most once. Only the pixel a coordinate takes differs between edits — brush paints its own pixel, erase keeps what is there and drops the alpha — so `paint` supplies that per pixel and the disc geometry lives here once, payload-free.

**Parameters**

- `surface` (`IEditSurface<TPixel>`) - The surface being edited; supplies bounds and any read-back the paint needs.
- `path` (`IReadOnlyList<(int, int)>`) - The gesture's pixel path; discs are stamped along it.
- `size` (`int`) - Disc diameter in pixels; anything below 1 is treated as 1.
- `paint` (`Func<int, int, TPixel>`) - What the pixel at a coordinate becomes.

**Returns.** The stamped pixels, deduplicated and clipped to the surface.

**Remarks**

The geometry, including joining the path so a fast stroke has no gaps, is [`Footprint.Discs()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.Footprint.md#m-discs-system-int32-system-int32-system-collections-gen-d0b472); this only projects it onto pixels.
